methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops delivered by a Norfolk native directly to Hampton Roads communities signals grassroots capability-building through peer networks, precisely the distributed, deep learning model that breaks metro concentration patterns.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab targets workplace professionals with structured training, creating institutional depth in a non-metro hub, but the college-centered delivery model may limit broader regional distribution beyond those who can access higher education programs.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates advanced AI education and innovation capacity in Richmond's institutional infrastructure, deepening metro capability but requiring intentional outreach mechanisms to avoid reinforcing the capital-region divide.

signals.title: Left hand, right hand: Virginia cools on data centers even as state policy promotes the AI that requires them - Cardinal News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's policy incoherence—promoting AI while localities resist the data center infrastructure AI requires—signals institutional fragmentation that prevents both deep capability development and distributed access, leaving the state stuck between competing visions.

signals.title: AI could predict droughts before they strike, Virginia Tech expert says - WSLS
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech researchers developing AI drought prediction demonstrates deep technical capability clustering around research universities, creating specialized excellence nodes that may or may not transfer to broader regional agricultural workforce applications.
